📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #18 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 08:37:08 AM IST
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT). Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others. One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR). Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players. “Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.” The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”. In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest. However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28. One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MS' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027;' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027;' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process." (Hinglish Arth: कई उद्योग निकाय वार्षिक बजट पूर्व परामर्श प्रक्रिया के हिस्से के रूप में वित्त मंत्रालय के शीर्ष अधिकारियों से मुलाकात कर रहे हैं)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने आग्रह किया कि समान अवसर सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कोई भी कर राहत सभी बोर्ड में समान रूप से लागू होनी चाहिए।)

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The two women so far are Alice Huang, who U.S. ‌intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health ‌care

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an ‌ intimate relationship with a second employee, according to ​two people familiar with the matter, Reuters has ⁠learned. The revelation follows two other extramarital affairs that led to his resignation Thursday. The two women are Alice Huang, who U.S. ‌intelligence suspects of being a Chinese spy, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health ‌care. Reuters is not naming the second employee. Attempts ‌to ⁠reach the woman were not successful. ALSO WATCH Watch: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid affair with alleged Chinese spy | Above the Fold | Nov 12, 2026 Nvidia declined to ⁠comment. Powell, Jensen Huang, and a representative for Nvidia’s board did not reply to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached ​for comment. Jensen Huang ‌admitted to an affair in a November 8 statement following the reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, without referring to her by name. The former Nvidia CEO’s ‌decision to resign from the company could disrupt ​the AI industry that he helped shape. Nvidia has used its financial strength to help ⁠create an industry around AI through complex financial arrangements that ease the purchase of the company’s chips. It has backed ‌cloud computing companies and AI labs in order to do so. Pressure on Jensen Huang, who is 63 and married, to resign mounted after reports of his affair with Alice Huang. Nvidia’s board appointed finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search ‌to replace Jensen Huang. The board is considering internal and external ​candidates for the job.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside ⁠legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by ⁠a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.

articles.title: UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28, countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity and transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP29 focused on energy storage, grid modernisation and climate finance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Clean public transport, energy-efficient buildings and affordable energy are a few of the things the president of the UN climate talks — known as COP31 — asked global leaders and climate activists to pledge as part of the global electrification plan laid out during the world's largest annual climate summit. But environmental and human rights organisations caution that without strong safeguards, the mining boom for the minerals and metals needed to make the power lines, batteries, wind turbines and other energy infrastructure that can make the pledge a reality could have serious environmental and human rights impacts across the globe. Mining has come at a cost to communities and habitats around the globe: Forests have been felled, water supplies poisoned and Indigenous peoples have lost access to land. Rights groups have urged COP31 officials to focus on how to fairly source the materials needed for the transition. Turkiye announced that electrification would be one of the main priorities during its copresidency of COP31 with Australia. The “35-by-35” global electrification pledge aims to increase the use of electricity from 21% to 35% by 2035 to reduce planet-warming greenhouse emissions, preferably from renewable energy such as solar and wind. The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28 , countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity and transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP29 focused on energy storage, grid modernisation and climate finance. The COP31 presidency said electrification is the next logical step, translating earlier pledges into changes in how energy is consumed. “This transition brings together renewable energy, strong grids, storage capacity, energy efficiency, clean transport and green industry. Each supports the others,” said COP31 president Murat Kurum, who is also Turkiye's environment minister. “We want people to feel the results of climate talks in daily life: in buildings that use less energy, in clean public transport, in energy they can afford and in new jobs.” Environmental activists note that the pledge does not require that electricity must come from renewable sources, meaning coal and other fossil fuels could be used. But as countries try to move away from fossil fuels, renewable energy is expected to play a major role.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: From Indonesia to Brazil, the boom in demand for the metals and minerals needed to create wind turbines, solar panels, electric vehicle batteries, high-speed railways and other technologies crucial for the renewable energy transition has been underway for some time, according to the International Energy Agency.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 08:20:37 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28, countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity and transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP29 focused on energy storage, grid modernisation and climate finance

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Clean public transport, energy-efficient buildings and affordable energy are a few of the things the president of the UN climate talks — known as COP31 — asked global leaders and climate activists to pledge as part of the global electrification plan laid out during the world's largest annual climate summit. But environmental and human rights organisations caution that without strong safeguards, the mining boom for the minerals and metals needed to make the power lines, batteries, wind turbines and other energy infrastructure that can make the pledge a reality could have serious environmental and human rights impacts across the globe. Mining has come at a cost to communities and habitats around the globe: Forests have been felled, water supplies poisoned and Indigenous peoples have lost access to land. Rights groups have urged COP31 officials to focus on how to fairly source the materials needed for the transition. Turkiye announced that electrification would be one of the main priorities during its copresidency of COP31 with Australia. The “35-by-35” global electrification pledge aims to increase the use of electricity from 21% to 35% by 2035 to reduce planet-warming greenhouse emissions, preferably from renewable energy such as solar and wind. The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28 , countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity and transitioning away from fossil fuels. COP29 focused on energy storage, grid modernisation and climate finance. The COP31 presidency said electrification is the next logical step, translating earlier pledges into changes in how energy is consumed. “This transition brings together renewable energy, strong grids, storage capacity, energy efficiency, clean transport and green industry. Each supports the others,” said COP31 president Murat Kurum, who is also Turkiye's environment minister. “We want people to feel the results of climate talks in daily life: in buildings that use less energy, in clean public transport, in energy they can afford and in new jobs.” Environmental activists note that the pledge does not require that electricity must come from renewable sources, meaning coal and other fossil fuels could be used. But as countries try to move away from fossil fuels, renewable energy is expected to play a major role.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: From Indonesia to Brazil, the boom in demand for the metals and minerals needed to create wind turbines, solar panels, electric vehicle batteries, high-speed railways and other technologies crucial for the renewable energy transition has been underway for some time, according to the International Energy Agency.

Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Electrification (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Electrification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Modernisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Modernisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28, countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'UN climate summit pushes electrification goal' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'UN climate summit pushes electrification goal' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The pledge builds on commitments made at previous UN climate summits: At COP28, countries agreed to work toward tripling renewable energy capacity..." (Hinglish Arth: यह प्रतिज्ञा पिछले संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु शिखर सम्मेलन में की गई प्रतिबद्धताओं पर आधारित है: COP28 में, देशों ने नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा क्षमता को तीन गुना करने और जीवाश्म ईंधन से दूर जाने की दिशा में काम करने पर सहमति व्यक्त की।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "UN climate summit pushes electrification goal as groups call for mining safeguards"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. From Indonesia to Brazil, the boom in demand for the metals and minerals needed to create wind turbines, solar panels, electric vehicle batteries,...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "From Indonesia to Brazil, the boom in demand for the metals and minerals needed to create wind turbines, solar panels, electric vehicle batteries,..." (Hinglish Arth: इंडोनेशिया से ब्राजील तक, पवन टरबाइन, सौर पैनल, इलेक्ट्रिक वाहन बैटरी, हाई-स्पीड रेलवे और नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा के लिए महत्वपूर्ण अन्य प्रौद्योगिकियों को बनाने के लिए आवश्यक धातुओं और खनिजों की मांग में उछाल)

articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea. The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile". He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations. Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage. A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack". The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night of having intercepted a drone in the Riyadh area. It previously said it had knocked down several other missiles and drones from Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night through Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, though it was unclear whether they were the ones mentioned by the Iran-backed group.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said it had intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region and another in Saudi Arabia's east.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 07:43:52 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea. The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile". He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations. Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage. A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack". The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night of having intercepted a drone in the Riyadh area. It previously said it had knocked down several other missiles and drones from Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night through Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, though it was unclear whether they were the ones mentioned by the Iran-backed group.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said it had intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region and another in Saudi Arabia's east.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea. The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile". He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful. The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations. Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage. A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack". The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night of having intercepted a drone in the Riyadh area. It previously said it had knocked down several other missiles and drones from Wednesday (November 11, 2026) night through Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, though it was unclear whether they were the ones mentioned by the Iran-backed group.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Thursday (November 12, 2026) morning, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said it had intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region and another in Saudi Arabia's east.

articles.title: U.S., Ukraine say Europe to join Russia talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday (November 12, 2026) Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war. In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Mr. Zelenskyy in Dublin. As they spoke to journalists on the tarmac of a military airbase in Ireland, the main piece of progress touted by the Ukrainian leader and U.S. President Donald Trump's representative was that European negotiators would be at the table for future talks. Mr. Zelenskyy said Europeans will take part rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines as they were in Abu Dhabi, insisting: "They will have a voice". Mr. Kushner later reiterated the sentiment in a post on X, writing: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners." "Significant differences remain, but we are encouraged by the progress made," he posted, adding that the schedule and details on the negotiating track would be released "shortly". An EU official told AFP representatives of five European capitals as well as the European Commission that the U.S. envoys, and that a new multilateral meeting "will be fixed soon". The Kremlin did not confirm Mr. Putin had agreed to include Europe in future talks, which Kyiv and its allies have long been seeking. Instead, the Russian leader had earlier told the U.S. duo he would not water down demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine -- a deployment he said would be a "continuation of war".
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As the United States has pushed for Europe to be allowed at the table, Moscow has sought to reframe talks as part of a wider discussion about European security.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 U.S., Ukraine say Europe to join Russia talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 07:33:27 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday (November 12, 2026) Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war. In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Mr. Zelenskyy in Dublin. As they spoke to journalists on the tarmac of a military airbase in Ireland, the main piece of progress touted by the Ukrainian leader and U.S. President Donald Trump's representative was that European negotiators would be at the table for future talks. Mr. Zelenskyy said Europeans will take part rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines as they were in Abu Dhabi, insisting: "They will have a voice". Mr. Kushner later reiterated the sentiment in a post on X, writing: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners." "Significant differences remain, but we are encouraged by the progress made," he posted, adding that the schedule and details on the negotiating track would be released "shortly". An EU official told AFP representatives of five European capitals as well as the European Commission that the U.S. envoys, and that a new multilateral meeting "will be fixed soon". The Kremlin did not confirm Mr. Putin had agreed to include Europe in future talks, which Kyiv and its allies have long been seeking. Instead, the Russian leader had earlier told the U.S. duo he would not water down demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine -- a deployment he said would be a "continuation of war".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As the United States has pushed for Europe to be allowed at the table, Moscow has sought to reframe talks as part of a wider discussion about European security.

articles.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26 new roads as part of ICBR-III

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu . Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said. The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details. This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China. The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China. The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh. Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh. The project clearance came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit from September 11 to 13 in New Delhi, which was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping. A government statement after the meeting said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. In December 2020, the MHA had approved construction of 18 pedestrian tracks, including foot suspension bridges, log bridges, and staging camps, measuring a total length of 598.27 km in the border areas of Arunachal Pradesh. On October 22 this year, former ITBP Director-General Shatrujeet Kapur mentioned that the “face-off” with Chinese troops “continues at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing the Himveer Samman Samaroah at the Central Training College at Alwar in Rajasthan, Mr. Kapur said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-offs happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues. Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 07:07:01 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26 new roads as part of ICBR-III

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu . Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said. The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details. This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China. The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China. The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh. Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh. The project clearance came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit from September 11 to 13 in New Delhi, which was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping. A government statement after the meeting said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues. In December 2020, the MHA had approved construction of 18 pedestrian tracks, including foot suspension bridges, log bridges, and staging camps, measuring a total length of 598.27 km in the border areas of Arunachal Pradesh. On October 22 this year, former ITBP Director-General Shatrujeet Kapur mentioned that the “face-off” with Chinese troops “continues at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Addressing the Himveer Samman Samaroah at the Central Training College at Alwar in Rajasthan, Mr. Kapur said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-offs happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues. Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”

Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Construction (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Construction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Tranquillity (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Tranquillity' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure al' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure al' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Indo-Tibetan Border Police sanctions the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; CCS clears 26..." (Hinglish Arth: भारत-तिब्बत सीमा पुलिस ने अरुणाचल प्रदेश में 15 पैदल यात्री सस्पेंशन पुलों और 18 लॉग पुलों के निर्माण को मंजूरी दी; सीसीएस ने आईसीबीआर-III के हिस्से के रूप में 26 नई सड़कों को मंजूरी दी)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”." (Hinglish Arth: हमारे शौर्य कमांडो ने इसमें अनुकरणीय भूमिका निभाई।”)

articles.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”; it determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps. Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether. Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services. Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications. In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.” Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks. Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix. “We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X. Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: technology (general) / internet / communication infrastructure / science and technology

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: On November 4, 2026, in the journal Nature, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University presented their findings on an Agentic laboratory platform, “AutoDNA”. It is an artificial intelligence system with agents performing the function of humans who usually perform complex experiments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In 2022, many of us would have made fun of the AI models when they made errors in identifying the capitals of popular countries accurately. Most of us took the stature of the rabbit and looked at artificial intelligence tools as a tortoise. But in four years’ time, what happened to the rabbit is now happening to humans.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A laboratory researcher, even in their wildest of their dreams would not have thought of witnessing a physical lab which can decide, plan and work on its own. It is now a reality. Most of us know how generative AI works. Humans hold the guide wire, sitting in front of the computer screen, and the chatbot’s response never comes out of the screen. The response can influence your brain, but cannot physically control your pen, paper or anything outside the computer. In contrast, has the capability to do independent physical activities. In a biology lab, it can command a pipette to take a fluid and transfer a few drops into a beaker, heat a tube with a thermal cycler, read the degree of fluorescence in a reaction, complete a series of experiments, observe and document the results and even interpret it.

articles.title: Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The child, diagnosed with Type II achalasia, underwent a minimally invasive procedure at Rela Hospital in Chennai

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An eight-year-old boy diagnosed with Type II achalasia – a rare disorder that affects the ability to swallow food and liquids – has undergone a Perora-l Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) procedure at Rela Hospital. Achalasia affects the nerves controlling the muscles of the oesophagus, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter – a muscular valve connecting the food pipe to the stomach – to remain abnormally tight. This prevents food and liquids from passing normally into the stomach. The condition is estimated to affect 0.1 to 0.18 children per 100,000 annually. The child had progressively worsening difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. Following the procedure, he was able to resume consuming clear liquids and subsequently, a soft diet, within 24 hours. POEM involves passing an endoscope through the mouth and creating a small tunnel within the oesophageal wall to reach and divide the muscle fibres causing the obstruction. Unlike conventional surgery, the procedure does not require external incisions or stitches. S.N.K. Chenduran, senior consultant and endoscopic surgeon, Department of Medical Gastroenterology, performed the procedure, which took about 50 minutes. He said performing POEM in children required particular precision because of the smaller dimensions of the oesophagus and the delicate tissues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Dinesh Jothimani, director, Hepatology and Medical Gastroenterology, said persistent swallowing difficulties, regurgitation, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss in children warranted medical evaluation.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (13 NOV)

📰 Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder

📌 Published: 13 Nov 2026, 12:10:25 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The child, diagnosed with Type II achalasia, underwent a minimally invasive procedure at Rela Hospital in Chennai

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An eight-year-old boy diagnosed with Type II achalasia – a rare disorder that affects the ability to swallow food and liquids – has undergone a Perora-l Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) procedure at Rela Hospital. Achalasia affects the nerves controlling the muscles of the oesophagus, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter – a muscular valve connecting the food pipe to the stomach – to remain abnormally tight. This prevents food and liquids from passing normally into the stomach. The condition is estimated to affect 0.1 to 0.18 children per 100,000 annually. The child had progressively worsening difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. Following the procedure, he was able to resume consuming clear liquids and subsequently, a soft diet, within 24 hours. POEM involves passing an endoscope through the mouth and creating a small tunnel within the oesophageal wall to reach and divide the muscle fibres causing the obstruction. Unlike conventional surgery, the procedure does not require external incisions or stitches. S.N.K. Chenduran, senior consultant and endoscopic surgeon, Department of Medical Gastroenterology, performed the procedure, which took about 50 minutes. He said performing POEM in children required particular precision because of the smaller dimensions of the oesophagus and the delicate tissues.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Dinesh Jothimani, director, Hepatology and Medical Gastroenterology, said persistent swallowing difficulties, regurgitation, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss in children warranted medical evaluation.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures. One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #3 of 30 (12 NOV)

📰 Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize

📌 Published: 12 Nov 2026, 08:04:02 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures. One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence

व्यावहारिक और धरातलीय — सिर्फ किताबी सिद्धांतों के बजाय ज़मीनी हकीकत और नतीजों पर काम करने वाला।
✓ Syn: Practical, Realistic, Utilitarian  |  ✖ Ant: Idealistic, Impractical, Utopian
Understandability (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Understandability' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Mathematical (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Mathematical' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Intelligence (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Intelligence' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Pri' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society." (Hinglish Arth: इस वर्ष का बुकर पुरस्कार समाज में एआई के स्थान के बारे में चिंता को दर्शाता है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "award-winning books / books and publishing / Artificial Intelligence." (Hinglish Arth: पुरस्कार विजेता पुस्तकें/किताबें और प्रकाशन/आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस)

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary. The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Maharashtra / Bharatiya Janata Party / government / Indian National Congress / politics

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.badge: Analytical Q1 • Central Inference & Passage Core
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Based on a critical reading of the above ✍️ Editorial & Opinion passage on "Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
options: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing.
Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Da' should be permanently discontinued.
The author contends that 'Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Da' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing." (Hinglish Arth: गोकुल डेयरी सहकारी समिति में शासनादेश का पलटना परेशान करने वाला है)

ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.badge: Analytical Q2 • Key Evidence, Policy & Way Forward
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.question: Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate"?
options: Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
Maharashtra / Bharatiya Janata Party / government / Indian National Congress / politics.
Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.answerText: Maharashtra / Bharatiya Janata Party / government / Indian National Congress / politics.
ultraAnalyticalQuestions2.hinglishExplanation: Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Maharashtra / Bharatiya Janata Party / government / Indian National Congress / politics." (Hinglish Arth: महाराष्ट्र/भारतीय जनता पार्टी/सरकार/भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस/राजनीति)

hinglishTracks.en: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — गोकुल डेयरी सहकारी समिति में शासनादेश का पलटना परेशान करने वाला है। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — चुनावी कदाचार को लेकर राष्ट्रव्यापी आक्रोश के बीच, हर दिन नए सबूत सामने आने के साथ, महाराष्ट्र में भाजपा सरकार एक कार्यकारी आदेश के माध्यम से एक लोकप्रिय जनादेश को पलटने में एक कदम आगे बढ़ गई है।।

hinglishTracks.en: It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — इसने 4 नवंबर को एक अध्यादेश के माध्यम से महाराष्ट्र सहकारी समिति अधिनियम को बदलने की मंजूरी दे दी - जिसे राज्यपाल ने 6 नवंबर को प्रख्यापित किया - भाजपा और उसके सहयोगियों द्वारा कोल्हापुर जिला सहकारी दूध उत्पादक संघ, जिसे गोकुल डेयरी के नाम से जाना जाता है, के अधिग्रहण की सुविधा के तत्काल प्रभाव से।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाले पैनल ने 19 अक्टूबर को सहकारी बोर्ड की 25 निर्वाचित सीटों में से 13 पर जीत हासिल की।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — गोकुल, जो महाराष्ट्र के सबसे प्रभावशाली सहकारी संस्थानों में से एक है, का वार्षिक कारोबार लगभग ₹4,000 करोड़ है और यह पश्चिमी महाराष्ट्र में कई लाख दूध उत्पादकों से जुड़ा हुआ है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — भाजपा ने गृह मंत्री अमित शाह के अधीन सहकारिता मंत्रालय बनाकर, अपने राजनीतिक प्रभुत्व के एक और क्षेत्र के रूप में सहकारी क्षेत्र पर अपनी नजरें गड़ा दी थीं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — जबकि सहकारी समितियों को नियंत्रित करने की योजना विभिन्न माध्यमों से चल रही है, कांग्रेस के नेतृत्व वाले विपक्ष द्वारा स्पष्ट रूप से जीते गए चुनाव को पलटना भाजपा द्वारा एक नए स्तर की निर्लज्जता और न्यायपालिका से उसके कार्यों को प्राप्त होने वाली दण्डमुक्ति का प्रतीक है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सतेज पाटिल के नेतृत्व वाली कांग्रेस समर्थित राजर्षि शाहू शेतकारी समविचारी अघाड़ी ने गोकुल बोर्ड की 25 निर्वाचित सीटों में से 13 पर जीत हासिल की।।

hinglishTracks.en: On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — 29 अक्टूबर को, भाजपा-सहयोगी सदस्यों के भाग नहीं लेने के बाद अध्यक्ष के चुनाव में गतिरोध आ गया था और बैठक में 14 सदस्यों की आवश्यक कोरम कम हो गई थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — कांग्रेस और उसके सहयोगियों से संबद्ध निदेशकों ने बाद में शशिकांत पाटिल चुयेकर को अध्यक्ष घोषित किया, लेकिन प्रशासन ने चुनाव को मान्यता देने से इनकार कर दिया क्योंकि कोरम की आवश्यकताएं पूरी नहीं हुई थीं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Administration' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — अध्यादेश के माध्यम से किए गए संशोधन ने सरकार को कुछ बड़े सहकारी संस्थानों में पांच निदेशकों को नामित करने की अनुमति दी, जिसमें चार नामांकित व्यक्तियों को मतदान का अधिकार प्राप्त हुआ।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — निश्चित रूप से, चार को गोकुल बोर्ड में तुरंत नामांकित किया गया था, और उन्होंने 10 नवंबर को अध्यक्ष चुनने के लिए भाजपा और उसके सहयोगियों के साथ मतदान किया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — सहकारी सदस्यों का जनादेश कांग्रेस और उसके सहयोगियों के पक्ष में 13-12 था, लेकिन राज्य सरकार द्वारा मतदान के अधिकार वाले सदस्यों की नियुक्ति के साथ, यह भाजपा और उसके सहयोगियों के पक्ष में 16-13 हो गया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Cooperative' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cooperative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — पराजित लोगों ने सरकार द्वारा मनोनीत निदेशकों को मतदान से रोकने के लिए 9 नवंबर को बॉम्बे उच्च न्यायालय का दरवाजा खटखटाया, लेकिन उच्च न्यायालय ने वह राहत नहीं दी।।

hinglishTracks.en: The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern .
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — लोकतांत्रिक सिद्धांतों के पक्ष में हस्तक्षेप करने में न्यायपालिका का संदेह चिंता का विषय बनता जा रहा है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — गोकुल डेयरी में लोकप्रिय जनादेश को पलटने को एक अलग घटना के रूप में नहीं देखा जा सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह राज्य सत्ता द्वारा लोगों की पसंद को खामोश करने के परेशान करने वाले पैटर्न का एक और उदाहरण है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Maharashtra / Bharatiya Janata Party / government / Indian National Congress / politics
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — महाराष्ट्र/भारतीय जनता पार्टी/सरकार/भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस/राजनीति।

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #4 of 30 (12 NOV)

📰 Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate

📌 Published: 12 Nov 2026, 07:19:19 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary. The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas. The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development. Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise. The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27. Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups.. “We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said. The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply. Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions. “Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.
