dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: India’s federal structure could have benefited from the Kurian Committee

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny. In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Tamil Nadu / government / politics / language / Delimitation / education / Governor / taxes and duties / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Bharatiya Janata Party

In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%. The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington. “But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI . The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs. Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India. Last month, the IMF raised India’s growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7%, from the 6.4% and 6.7% projections respectively made in July. “India does remain a key growth engine for the world. The economy has strong fundamentals and has shown considerable resilience,” Ms. Kozack said.

Veeramani has already filed the first charge sheet in one of the multiple cases registered against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, and other laws, State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan told the Madras High Court on Thursday (November 12, 2026). Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP said, the first charge sheet in the case was filed before the special court for POCSO cases in Chennai on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) and that the SIT intends to file multiple charge sheets in some of the cases. He told the court that the charge sheets in other crime numbers would also be filed one after another in the next 10 to 15 days. Gem Granites Veeramani’s daughter Archana moves Madras High Court alleging human rights violations by SIT Police seize third video allegedly showing ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani abusing minor After hearing him, the judge adjourned a couple of connected writ petitions pending before him to November 30, 2026. He also perused a status report filed on behalf of the SIT, explaining to the court the progress made in the investigation so far, and told the counsel present in the court that he was satisfied with the substantial work done in the sensitive case related to sexual exploitation of children. The judge directed the High Court Registry to keep the status report in safe custody and produce it before the court during the next hearing. The SIT had been filing periodical status reports ever since journalist R. Varaaki and advocate M.L. Ravi filed writ petitions (criminal) in the High Court, seeking the transfer of investigation in the POCSO cases against Veeramani from the State police to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Fresh sexual harassment complaint against ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani Special Public Prosecutors appointed to conduct trial in POCSO Act cases against Veeramani After not finding any reason to order such transfer for the present, the judge had said that the SIT must be allowed to work in peace and called for periodical status reports on the ongoing investigation. When Mr. Varaaki’s counsel presented some evidence before the court on Thursday, the judge directed the petitioner to submit all those materials with the SIT instead of waiting for the court proceedings.

3. dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The Ladakh administration shifted the activist from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk on Thursday (November 12, 2026) described the restrictions imposed by the administration on him as “bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate” and conspicuously “not using words such as house arrest”. Invoking Section 163(1) of the BNSS, the Ladakh administration on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) evening shifted Mr. Wangchuk from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence. “I was driven towards my village, where my residence is and was eventually taken to HIAL, reaching there at approximately 8.40 p.m. [on Wednesday]. I was told to remain at home under the supervision of police guards. Since that evening, dozens of armed police personnel [approximately 20 to 22] have been stationed at and around my residence,” said Mr. Wangchuk in a letter to senior officials of Ladakh and the Union Home Ministry. Referring to the order issued by the Additional District Magistrate, Leh, Mr. Wangchuk said it disclosed no reasons justifying the necessity or proportionality of such an extended restriction, nor does it identify any continuing emergency or threat attributable to me that would warrant restraints of such duration.” “The actions have clearly been taken to curtail my movement and rights before the election. The order is clearly bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate. I request you to kindly offer the clarification at the earliest, and withdraw this order without delay,” said Mr. Wangchuk, in the letter. He claimed there was “no explicit order of house arrest or directing deployment of police personnel was shown to me then, and none has been served on me since”. “I have not sought any security cover, and I am not aware of any threat to my person. No written order authorising this deployment has been furnished to me, and I do not know who directed it, on what date, or under what provision of law. I would be grateful to be informed of these particulars,” he added. The Ladakh activist, who was arrested in September last year under the National Security Act (NSA) and released in March this year, said the Ladakh administration’s order “conspicuously does not use words such as “house arrest”. “It does not use the words “detention” or “confinement”. It nowhere directs me to remain at my residence — a direction given orally to me by the personnel who picked me up and are now present outside my house. The order does not mention the scope or extent of the restrictions imposed on my movement, leaving their implementation to the discretion of the police personnel deployed,” said Mr. Wangchuk.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The alleged restrictions on Mr. Wanghuk came when Ladakh was preparing to hold polls for panchayat and municipality on November 21 and for hill councils on December 4. However, Ladakh’s key civil society bodies, Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), have organised protests and demanded postponement of council elections to April-May next year.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: For generations, coconut trees have been more than just crops for the people in the coastal districts of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, and West Godavari. They have been their livelihood. However, two cyclones that hit the coastal district of Andhra Pradesh within the span of a week have left the coconut growers, farmers and fishing communities in the region staring down the barrel as thousands of coconut trees were flattened, lakhs of acres of paddy fields were wiped out, and dozens of boats became dysfunctional. Konaseema district has witnessed the swath of destruction, with over 73,500 coconut trees uprooted and paddy destroyed across 1,18,109 acres, leaving around 88,000 farmers in tatters. Meanwhile, in West Godavari district, 27,397 coconut trees were destroyed, affecting more than 5,000 small and marginal growers. Andhra Pradesh was ravaged by two cyclones between October 28 and November 3. One was a ‘Very Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) Arnab and the other, a ‘Severe’ Cyclonic Storm (SCS) Murasu, leaving the districts of West Godavari, Konaseema, and Bapatla in ruins, while Guntur, East Godavari and Palnadu were also affected, according to the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority. Coastal areas in two districts of West Godavari and Konaseema were ravaged by violent gales of around 150 kmph at the time of Arnab’s landfall on October 28 and 29, and suffered once again when extremely heavy rainfall pounded the districts on November 3 and 4 after Murasu made landfall near Ongole.

itemListElement.headline: Twin cyclone leave livelihoods in tatters
itemListElement.description: 1. Core Context & Background: Cyclones, Arnab and Murasu, which hit the Andhra Pradesh coastline within a span of a week, delivered a severe blow to the fisherfolk communities, coconut and casuarina growers in West Godavari and Konaseema districts, many of whom may have to look for alternative livelihoods for two to three years, writes Nellore Sravani
